method: Pages loaded with curl (UA IntrepidApp-Curation/1.0), about 1 req/s, text extracted and numerics re-read from the page. Verdicts: ok = supported as drafted; fix = supported only after the corrected text; cut = remove the claim; unverified = could not load the source (403/captcha), keep out or flag. 'primary' = drafts.json 'proposed'.

headline_errors_in_drafts: wellington-18 Red Rocks: 4.7 km / 1.5 h belongs to the WellingtonNZ 'Red Rocks Track' that starts at Waimapihi Reserve in Brooklyn, NOT to the walk from the Te Kopahou visitor centre at Owhiro Bay. The proposed bio attaches the wrong distance and time to the wrong start. Cut the numbers.

wellington-13 Matiu/Somes: 'predator-free' and 'former quarantine station' were cut as unsourced, but both ARE on loaded pages (DOC: 'predator-free scientific reserve'; East by West: 'functioned as a quarantine station'). The cuts were wrong; restore. The '75 minutes' loop could not be confirmed (brochure PDF text not extractable); cut or mark unverified.

wellington-19 Katherine Mansfield: 'born in 1888' and 'restored' were removed as unsourced, but the site's own /about pages say she was born 14 Oct 1888 at 25 Tinakori Road (the house, built 1888 by her father) and the house was returned to its original layout after the 1987 purchase. Restore the birth claim; say 'original layout', not 'Victorian state'.
wellington-2 Cable Car: draft says 'funicular' is not stated by sources; the cable car homepage says 'the last historic funicular in Aotearoa New Zealand'. The old word was supported.
wellington-9 Waterfront: '30 minutes one way' is not what the source says (freewalks: 1.2 km, 30 min to 2 h, extendable to 5+ km).

wellington-16 Wellington Museum: international visitors are charged (page: 'Free General Admission. International visitor charges apply'), so free: true is wrong for the app's audience; the amount could not be found.

wellington-27/wellington-6: adding wiki titles would change spotPhotoTitle and orphan the existing WIKI_IMAGE_OVERRIDES keys 'Weta Workshop' and 'Pencarrow Lighthouse'. Do not add them (both already resolve).
unverified_not_loadable: DOC Matiu brochure PDF (text not extractable)

items.note: Wikipedia: 'the world's southernmost capital of a sovereign state' and 'With a latitude of 41 17 South, Wellington is the southernmost capital city in the world'. Wikivoyage: 'very compact and pedestrian-friendly'. Supported.

Wikipedia: 'The city has served as New Zealand's capital since 1865' (parliament first met there on 26 July 1865; capital moved 1865). Status is by convention, not legislation; 'has been the capital since 1865' is fine.

Wikipedia says Wellington 'is more densely populated than most other cities in New Zealand due to the restricted amount of land that is available between its harbour and the steep hills'. That is about the city, not specifically the centre.
items.corrected: Limited land between harbour and hills makes Wellington denser than most New Zealand cities, and the Golden Mile from the railway station to Courtenay Place is easy to walk.

items.note: Wikivoyage: 'Golden Mile' runs from the Railway Station down Lambton Quay to Willis, Manners St and Courtenay Place, 'a diverting and pleasant walking route'. Wikipedia describes it as the bus corridor Railway Station to Courtenay Place.
Wikipedia: HQ Miramar, Wellington; tours confirmed on wetaworkshop.com/tours/wellington (1 Weka Street, Miramar).
Wikipedia: 'known for its bohemian nature', 'cafés, op-shops, music venues, restaurants, record shops'. 'Live music' is not stated; 'music venues' is.
items.corrected: Cuba Street is the bohemian strip of cafés, bars and music venues.

items.note: 'easily the most walkable city in the country' rightly removed (unsourced superlative). 'climbing steep green hills' is loosely supported (Wikipedia: 'green hillsides adorned with tiered suburbs'), and Wikivoyage says Wellington has 'more cafés, bars and restaurants per head than New York City', so 'lively food scene' was supportable; removal is fine but not required.
Matches the cable car homepage (Lambton Quay to Kelburn, views). No factual issue.

Wikipedia: 'Wellington is the world's windiest city, with an average wind speed of 27 km/h (17 mph)' and nickname 'Windy Wellington'. The 'guides say pack a windproof layer' attribution rests on the Intrepid page, which I did not load; if kept, drop 'guides say'.
items.corrected: Wellington is nicknamed Windy Wellington, with an average wind speed of 27 km/h, so pack a windproof layer in every season.

items.note: Wikivoyage: 'Remember to tag when you board the bus and as you leave the bus, or you will be charged for the whole route.' Snapper cards and contactless accepted on buses and trains.

tepapa.govt.nz/visit: 'International visitor museum entry ... aged 16 years and older (NZ$35). Entry to the museum remains free for all New Zealanders and people living in New Zealand.' Footer: 'paid exhibitions and experiences' may charge extra. Free group is New Zealanders AND residents; the draft says only New Zealanders.
items.corrected: Te Papa is free for New Zealanders and people living in New Zealand but costs NZ$35 for international visitors aged 16 and over, and some exhibitions charge extra.

items.note: Not re-derived (climate table figures 231.8 h / 20.6C not re-opened); wording makes no month-specific numeric claim beyond 'January sunniest, February warmest'. Left as unverified-numeric low risk; re-open Wikipedia climate box if the owner wants the figures kept.

'World's largest specimen of the colossal squid' is on Wikipedia (Te Papa article), NOT on tepapa.govt.nz/visit (which says only 'the colossal squid'). Source attribution in reason is wrong; claim itself is supported. Earthquake house simulation: Wikipedia, supported. National art collection: Te Papa visit page, supported.
items.corrected: New Zealand's national museum, with Māori and Pacific treasures, the national art collection, an earthquake house simulation and the world's largest colossal squid specimen.

items.note: NZ$35, aged 16+, confirmed on tepapa.govt.nz/visit and Wikipedia ('Te Papa charges an entrance fee of $35'). costMin 0 / costMax 35 / NZD OK; remove free:true. Hours 10am-6pm daily except Christmas Day confirmed, so specialClosures 25 Dec OK.
200; page text 'Home | Te Papa Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa'.

609 m and 1902 confirmed on wellingtoncablecar.co.nz ('Track length: 609 metres', 'Originally built in 1902'); Cable Car Museum named on the site. 'Funicular' IS stated ('the last historic funicular in Aotearoa New Zealand'), so the draft's reason is wrong and the word can stay.
items.corrected: A 609 m funicular from Lambton Quay up to Kelburn, first built in 1902, with a Cable Car Museum at the top.

items.note: Timetable page: Mon-Thu 7:30am-8:00pm, Fri 7:30am-9:00pm, Sat 8:30am-9:00pm, Sun & public holidays 8:30am-7:00pm; cars every 10 minutes; open every day except Christmas Day. Draft string matches except it omits 'public holidays' on the Sunday hours; add it.

Visitors: one-way adult $7.00, return adult $13.00 (child 5-15 $3.50/$6.50). The Spring Sundays $3 promo runs 6 Sep-18 Oct 2026 (after 3pm Sundays) and does not change the standard fare. costMin 7 / costMax 13 correct.

Wikipedia: 225 ha; 8.6 km pest-exclusion fence; kākā, little spotted kiwi, takahē and 70 tuatara released. Draft says 'predator-proof fence' which the article also uses. Tūī not named, rightly removed.

visitzealandia.com, www.zealandia.com and the rezdy listing all return 403/Cloudflare to scripts. NZ$26-31 cannot be confirmed from a loadable source. Wikipedia only confirms 9am-5pm daily except 25 December. Keep the existing ticketUrl but flag for browser check; do not publish 26-31 as verified. The booking-required tip was rightly dropped.

MediaWiki API: article exists (71,675 bytes, not a disambiguation, no redirect). The current 'Mount Victoria, Wellington' redirects to the 'Mount Victoria' disambiguation page (1,161 bytes). No WIKI_IMAGE_OVERRIDES key uses either title (grepped), so renaming is safe, but the image manifest entry keyed by the old title must be rebuilt.

wellingtongardens.nz: '25 hectares'; 'official Wellington Botanic Garden was established in 1868'; 'Lady Norwood Rose Garden (1953) has more than 300 varieties of roses ... at their best November-March'. All confirmed.

Grounds 'Year-round | Dawn to Dusk' confirmed; visitor centre hours as drafted. ticketUrl loads, title 'Wellington Gardens | Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā'. Rose Garden car park paid, limited to 2 h: confirmed. No entry charge stated.

Both 'Wētā Workshop' (60,643 bytes) and 'Weta Workshop' (redirect to it) resolve. Existing override key is 'Weta Workshop' (imageOverrides.ts line 250: 'The Weta Cave.jpg'); adding wiki would change spotPhotoTitle and orphan that override. Do not add the field.
Wikipedia: HQ Miramar; 'Academy Award-winning work on The Lord of the Rings film trilogy'. Tours: 1 Weka Street, Miramar. 'Oscar-winning' is a fair paraphrase.

Tour page: 'Open hours 7 days (except Christmas Day)'; Wētā Workshop Experiences tour 'From $59 NZD' (90-minute tour referenced on the transfer product at From $105). Price is a 'from' price, so costMin/costMax 59 is approximate; fine.
parliament.nz and www3.parliament.nz serve a Radware captcha to scripts. 'free guided tours of about an hour run daily' is unconfirmed by me. Keep ticketUrl out. Safer bio avoids the tour length.
items.corrected: The seat of government, where the Beehive and Parliament House stand together, with free guided tours.

items.note: API: 'Wellington Waterfront' redirects to 'Wellington Harbour'; 'Wellington waterfront' (lowercase w, current wiki value) is not a separate article. Removing wiki and adding an override keyed 'Wellington Waterfront' is correct.

freewalks.nz: Writers Walk 'Distance: 1.2 km (can be extended to 5+ km) | Time: 30 minutes - 2 hours', '23 typographical sculptures', walk 'stretches from Kumutoto Stream ... to Oriental Bay'; Solace in the Wind named. The '30 minutes one way' figure is not stated. The old bio's Te Papa to Oriental Bay is also roughly right.
items.corrected: A harbourside walk from Kumutoto Stream to Oriental Bay, lined with sculptures such as Solace in the Wind and the 23 quotes of the Wellington Writers Walk.

items.note: Wikipedia: opened 1906, 'oldest public zoo in New Zealand'; 'close encounters with ... giraffes, meerkats, lemurs and big cats'; hospital The Nest Te Kōhanga lets the public watch the vets; nocturnal house closed 2021 after the last kiwi (Tahi) died. 'No kiwi' removal and 'kiwi house' cut are correct. Sumatran tigers / red pandas not confirmed (zoo site 403).

wellingtonzoo.com, www.wellingtonzoo.com, wellingtonzoo.com/plan-your-visit and the newzealand.com listing all return 403. NZ$28/35 and 9:30-5 cannot be confirmed. Do not change the existing cost (29) to 28-35 on the strength of an unloaded page, or mark approximate; keep the ticketUrl but flag for a browser check.

Whitireia Park and Aotea Lagoon are in the Wikipedia article. 'Te Araroa trail passing through' does not appear in the loaded Porirua article (0 hits), and newzealand.com/nz/porirua 403s. Cut the Te Araroa clause unless sourced.
items.corrected: A city wrapped around Porirua Harbour, with headland walks at Whitireia Park and Aotea Lagoon beside the water.

items.note: wellingtongardens.nz/otari-wiltons-bush: 'only public botanic garden in New Zealand dedicated solely to native plants'; 'around 11 kilometres of walking tracks'; 'farmer Job Wilton chose to protect seven hectares of original forest'; Canopy Walkway named. ticketUrl loads, title 'Wellington Gardens | Ōtari-Wilton's Bush'.

DOC: 'predator-free scientific reserve'; 'gentle walking track takes you around the 24.8-hectare island'; 'little blue penguins' among species. East by West: it 'has functioned as a quarantine station, internment camp, and military site'; DOC: 'the historic maximum security animal quarantine building is closed'. Ferry runs Queens Wharf and Days Bay. The '75 minutes' loop is not on the DOC page or East by West page; I could not extract the brochure text, so it is unverified.
items.corrected: A 24.8-hectare predator-free DOC reserve and former quarantine station in Wellington Harbour, reached by East by West ferry from Queens Wharf or Days Bay, with a walking track around the island and little blue penguins.

items.note: DOC: 'The island and Visitor Centre are open daily between 8:30 am and 5:00 pm'; 'may be closed to visitors at times of extreme fire danger'. East by West: bookings are required for day trips and the ferry runs seven days a week. Add 'booking required' to the qualifier if space allows.

East by West (valid from 15 May 2026): Return Adult $42, includes a $6 visitor fee; child $24; SuperGold $6. costMin/costMax 42, NZD confirmed. Note: the sheet shows one adult price for both Queens Wharf and Days Bay.

DOC page loads (200), title 'Matiu/Somes Island Scientific and Historic Reserve: Places to go in Wellington and Kapiti'; East by West page also loads, title 'Mātiu / Somes Island | East by West Ferries'.
Wikipedia: 2004 renovation with 22,000 tonnes of sand shipped from Golden Bay (so 'early 2000s' is right); Norfolk pines are a listed point of interest. 'Palm-lined' unsupported; correctly removed.

museumswellington.org.nz/wellington-museum/: 'Our visiting hours are 10am to 5pm, 7 days a week. Free General Admission. International visitor charges apply.' admission-changes page: fee for international visitors from 1 Oct 2024, 'not charged for New Zealand residents'. The international price is not published on any page I could load. So free:true is wrong for international users. 1892 Bond Store and Wahine Theatre confirmed. Recommend dropping free:true and costMin 0, costMax unknown (omit costMax until confirmed) or flag for owner.
items.corrected: A museum in the 1892 Bond Store on the waterfront, with a Wellington timeline, maritime history and the Wahine Theatre's film of the 1968 Wahine disaster; free for New Zealand residents, with a charge for international visitors.

items.note: Loads, title 'Wellington Museum'.

Wikipedia: Days Bay 'walled on three sides by steep bush-clad slopes'; Day's Bay Pavilion opened Nov 1897 and 'totally destroyed' by fire Oct 1952, 'eventually replaced by a small building'; the story 'At the Bay' was based on Mansfield's childhood holidays there. Pavilion removal correct. The ferry from Queens Wharf is from East by West.

WRONG ATTRIBUTION. wellingtonnz.com Red Rocks Track (4.7 km, 1 hr 30 min, 135 m climb, 533 m descent) 'starts from the southern end of the Barking Emu track in Waimapihi Reserve' in Brooklyn and heads down to the coast; the Owhiro Bay walk is separate ('follow the coastline on the Red Rocks Coastal Walk to Owhiro Bay'). Wikipedia only says access is 'along a walking track from Te Kopahou Reserve visitor centre in Ōwhiro Bay' with seals at Sinclair Head 'just beyond Red Rocks'. The 4.7 km / 1.5 h each way figure cannot be used for the Owhiro Bay walk. Also: the Red Rocks reserve is 0.52 ha. Seal removal to Turakirae is the owner's call; Turakirae does have the larger documented colony (DOC: 'largest NZ fur seal colony in the Wellington region').
items.corrected: A coastal walk from the Te Kopahou Reserve visitor centre at Owhiro Bay to the red rock formation in a small scientific reserve on Wellington's south coast, with fur seals at Sinclair Head just beyond.

items.note: katherinemansfield.com/about/katherine-mansfield: 'born Kathleen Mansfield Beauchamp at 11 (later renumbered to 25) Tinakori Road, Thorndon on 14 October 1888'. /about/the-house: house built for the family in 1888; 'returned to its original layout following its purchase in 1987'. So both removed claims are supported; 'Victorian state' is not the site's wording.
items.corrected: The Thorndon house where the writer Katherine Mansfield was born in 1888, a Category 1 Historic Place returned to its original layout, with a garden.

items.note: hours-and-admission: 'open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am-4pm ... closed on Mondays and most public holidays including New Year's Day, Day after New Year's Day, Easter Friday [sic], Christmas Day and Boxing Day'. Adults $10, concession $8, under-18s free. closedDays [1], costMin 8, costMax 10 correct. Old 'closed Mon-Tue' was wrong.
Loads, title 'Katherine Mansfield House & Garden'.

Wikipedia: 'seaside village, 20 minutes drive from the suburb of Karori'; 'suitable for fishing and diving'; '7 km walkway managed by the Department of Conservation ... follows the beach ... through farmland up to historic gun [emplacements]'.

City Gallery site (citygallery.org.nz and /visit/) now gives 67 Victoria Street, Mon-Sun 10am-5pm, Thursday until 9pm, with 'BOOK TICKETS' on the current exhibition and no mention of free entry. WellingtonNZ also lists 67 Victoria Street and says 'gallery entry is free' and 'permanent home is currently closed while buildings around Ngākau Civic Square are being renovated and earthquake strengthened'. So free:true is single-sourced and contradicted by a 'book tickets' prompt; the pin at Civic Square is probably the closed building. Founded 1980 per WellingtonNZ and Wikipedia.
items.corrected: A contemporary art gallery that opened in 1980 as the Wellington City Art Gallery and has shown exhibitions at its Victoria Street venue while its Civic Square building is closed for earthquake strengthening.

items.note: Loads, title 'Home - City Gallery'.

WellingtonNZ: 'Built in 2015, the park ... commemorates the First World War centenary'; Tomb of the Unknown Warrior; bronze sculptures; 'eight international memorials ... from Australia, Turkey, the United Kingdom, France, the United States, Belgium, Germany, and the Pacific Islands'. That is eight memorials, not eight countries (the last is the Pacific Islands). Building open 12-4pm Sat-Sun (autumn/winter) or Thu-Sun (spring/summer).
items.corrected: A memorial park built in 2015 for the First World War centenary around the National War Memorial, with the Tomb of the Unknown Warrior, bronze sculptures and eight international memorials.

items.note: museumswellington.org.nz/space-place/: full-dome planetarium, telescopes 'weather permitting', galleries on 'space, science, Matariki' and Māori navigation; adult $16, NZ student/Gold Card $14, child $10, family $49, 0-3 free; closed Christmas Day. Term time (13 Oct-13 Dec): Mon closed, Tue/Wed 5-10:30pm, Thu 10am-10:30pm, Fri/Sat 10am-11pm, Sun 10am-5pm; school holidays (14 Dec-7 Feb) Monday 10-5. Draft reason text for Tue/Wed is garbled but the page agrees with it. Hours string 'Varies by day; evening sessions most days' is fine. Admission page title is 'Space Place'; draft title 'Te Ara Whānui ki te Rangi | Space Place' is the page heading.

DOC: 'five earthquake-raised beaches', 'continuous record ... over the past 7,000 years', 'Up to 500 New Zealand fur seals stay at Turakirae Head each winter', 'about 45 minutes to walk to Turakirae Head' (from the car park 300 m before the end). Wikipedia says four ridges; DOC says five. Use DOC (managing agency). 'About 7,000 years of uplift' is a fair paraphrase.

Wikipedia: peaks to 456 m (Belmont Trig); first two concrete gravity dams in NZ built on Korokoro Stream 1903 and 1904; WWII ammunition stores and Belmont Trig views per GW page (research). Free entry: GW page lists only camping fees and a horse permit.

dowse.org.nz is behind a Cloudflare challenge; hours and closure rest on a search snippet. Do not publish 10-5 / closed Monday as verified. Wikipedia history claim (1971 opening, 1982 rename, 2013 remodel) not re-opened by me.

API: 'Pencarrow Lighthouse' is the real article (6,670 bytes); 'Pencarrow Head Lighthouse' redirects to it. No wiki field is needed; adding one would orphan the override key 'Pencarrow Lighthouse' (imageOverrides.ts line 318). Do not add it.

Wikipedia (Pencarrow Head): first permanent lighthouse in NZ, constructed 1859; 'New Zealand's only female lighthouse keeper, Mary Bennett, worked here'; four-hour return walk from Eastbourne. The ~8 km gravel track figure comes from tripideas.nz (not re-loaded by me).
huttcity.govt.nz is blocked to scripts; Wed-Sun 10-4 is from a snippet. Leave hours as 'Check operator for hours'. petonesettlers.org.nz must not be used (draft's warning stands).

pataka.org.nz: 'Open: 10am-5pm, 7 days a week', 'Free admission', address corner Norrie & Parumoana streets, Porirua; title 'Pataka home - pataka.org.nz'. Wikipedia building/Japanese garden claim not re-opened.

makarapeak.bike: '250 hectares of regenerating native bush', 'over 50 kilometres of ... single track', title 'Mākara Peak Mountain Bike Park'. 'Wellington's premier' not used. Free entry not stated; donations/volunteers noted.

Rightly removed: 'palm-lined' (Oriental Bay), 'historic pavilion' (Days Bay), kiwi house (Zoo), 'closed Mon-Tue' (Mansfield), 'Open 24 hours' (Botanic Garden), 'earthquake simulators' as plural, tūī at Zealandia, 'on Petone Wharf' needs owner check. WRONGLY removed: Matiu 'predator-free' and 'former quarantine station'; Mansfield 'born in 1888' (and 'restored'); cable car 'funicular'. Over-cautious removal elsewhere: Wellington 'lively food scene' (Wikivoyage supports it).
